content:
Apple is celebrating its 50th anniversary this year, and many customers are older than the company itself. Apple has launched a new support page listing 50 ways to make their devices easier to use, primarily through various accessibility settings.

From adjusting text size on your Apple Watch to having your iPhone alert you when the washing machine finishes its cycle, these tips cover a wide range of uses...

Apple says the company is committed to making its technology accessible to everyone, including older users.

At Apple, we believe the best technology should serve everyone — including older users. That's why our products and services are built with inclusivity at their core — built-in accessibility features that help you connect, create, and engage with what matters most to you, in whatever way works best for you. Life keeps changing, and so does the way we interact with the world. From enlarging onscreen text to making conversations clearer in noisy restaurants, Apple's ecosystem of devices, features, and services is designed to flexibly meet your needs.

The support page mainly introduces various accessibility features and is divided into ten main categories.

  • Vision: See your screen more comfortably
  • Hearing: Stay connected to conversations, alerts, and your surroundings
  • Mobility: Customise how you browse and operate your device
  • Speech: Express yourself your way
  • Cognition: Stay focused and in control
  • Personalisation: Create a one-of-a-kind experience
  • Organisation: Keep track of what matters
  • Health: Keep an eye on your wellbeing with practical insights
  • Safety: Enjoy peace of mind
  • Communication: Stay connected

Taking the Vision category as an example — it includes features such as enlarging text, bolding text, inverting colours, setting colour filters, reducing transparency, increasing contrast, and reducing on-screen motion. Some features, such as Sound Recognition, received a big push when they first launched but remain relatively unknown to this day.

Sound Recognition detects specific sounds and uses on-device intelligence to notify you when they're detected. The feature can recognise 15 different sounds, and can also be trained to recognise your name, as well as unique electronic sounds in your environment, such as beeps from kitchen appliances, specific types of alarms, or doorbells. On HomePod, Sound Recognition can also detect the sound of smoke or carbon monoxide alarms. Sound Recognition also works with CarPlay — your iPhone will listen for and detect sirens, car horns, and even a baby's cry. When a specific sound is detected, you'll receive a notification — and if you're using CarPlay, the notification will appear on your car's display.

This page is an excellent and comprehensive overview of the rich accessibility features currently available on Apple devices. Each section provides guidance according to supported devices, which may include iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV, Vision Pro, and CarPlay, depending on the feature.
